examples.ko: 저는 경제관념이 없어서 돈이 금방 없어져요.
examples.en: I have no sense of economy, so my money disappears quickly.
We teach our child a sense of money management from a young age.
A sense of economy starts with managing your allowance.
I asked a friend who is good with money for advice.
He lacks a sense of economy and has no plan either.
I heard the school gives lessons on money sense.

explain: '경제관념이 있다/없다/투철하다/부족하다'처럼 써요. 무조건 아끼는 '절약'과 달리 돈의 가치를 알고 계획적으로 쓰는 마음을 말해요. 돈을 헤프게 쓰는 사람에게 '경제관념이 없다'고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used as '경제관념이 있다/없다/투철하다/부족하다'. Unlike '절약', which is simply saving, it means knowing the value of money and spending with a plan. For someone who spends carelessly, people say '경제관념이 없다'.

examples.ko: 고액권을 잔돈으로 바꿔 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you change this large bill into small change?

examples.ko: 지갑에 고액권만 있어서 버스를 못 탔어요.
examples.en: I only had large bills in my wallet, so I couldn't take the bus.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 고액권을 받지 않는다고 해요.
examples.en: I heard this shop does not accept large bills.

examples.ko: 고액권 지폐에는 위조를 막는 기능이 더 많아요.
examples.en: Large-denomination notes have more anti-counterfeiting features.
I exchanged large bills for small ones at the bank.

examples.ko: 고액권이 나오고 나서 현금 쓰기가 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Using cash became more convenient after the large bills came out.

explain: 반대말은 '소액권'이에요. 가게에서 '큰돈'이나 '큰 지폐'라고도 말하고, '고액권을 잔돈으로 바꾸다'가 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is '소액권' (small-denomination bill). In shops people also say '큰돈' or '큰 지폐', and '고액권을 잔돈으로 바꾸다' is a very common phrase.

examples.en: The government announced an austerity policy this year.
The company got into trouble, so it switched to a tight budget.
Because of the belt-tightening, salaries didn't go up.
Our household is in austerity mode these days too.
When the economy gets worse, every country goes into austerity.
If austerity drags on, people's spending falls.

explain: 뉴스에서는 '긴축 정책', '긴축 재정'처럼 나라나 회사가 돈 쓰는 것을 줄일 때 써요. 가정에서는 '긴축 모드'처럼 농담 섞어 말하기도 해요. 반대 방향의 말은 '확장'이에요.
explain_en: In the news it appears as '긴축 정책' or '긴축 재정' when a country or company cuts spending. At home people sometimes say '긴축 모드' jokingly. The opposite direction is '확장' (expansion).

examples.en: How much is the tax I have to pay this year?
The tax amount differs depending on income.
The tax amount is written separately on the receipt.
If you get deductions, the tax amount goes down.

examples.ko: 세액을 계산해 주는 프로그램을 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a program that calculates the tax amount.

examples.ko: 신고서에 세액을 잘못 적어서 다시 냈어요.
examples.en: I wrote the wrong tax amount on the return, so I filed it again.

explain: '세금'은 세금 전체를 말하고, '세액'은 실제로 내야 하는 금액 숫자를 가리켜서 계산서, 신고서, 영수증에서 많이 보여요. '세액 공제'처럼 세금 용어와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '세금' is tax in general, while '세액' is the actual number you have to pay, so you see it on invoices, tax returns and receipts. It often appears in tax terms such as '세액 공제' (tax credit).

examples.ko: 이번 달은 보너스까지 받아서 정말 수지맞았어요.
examples.en: I got a bonus this month too, so I really came out ahead.

examples.ko: 싸게 산 가방이 알고 보니 명품이라니, 수지맞았네요.
examples.en: The bag I bought cheap turned out to be a luxury brand. What a bargain!

examples.ko: 친구 덕분에 공짜로 여행을 다녀와서 수지맞은 기분이에요.
examples.en: I got to go on a trip for free thanks to my friend, so I feel like I came out ahead.

examples.ko: 이 가격에 밥까지 주다니 수지맞는 장사네요.
examples.en: Meals included at this price? That's a profitable deal.

examples.ko: 쿠폰을 쓰면 훨씬 더 수지맞을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use a coupon, you can come out much further ahead.

examples.ko: 오늘 장사가 잘돼서 수지맞았다고 사장님이 웃으셨어요.
examples.en: The owner smiled and said business was good today and they had made a nice profit.

explain: 주로 '수지맞았어요', '수지맞는 장사'처럼 이익을 봤을 때 가볍게 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '이득을 보다'가 있고, '횡재하다'는 뜻밖의 큰 이익을 얻었을 때 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in casual forms like '수지맞았어요' or '수지맞는 장사' when you come out ahead. '이득을 보다' is similar, and '횡재하다' is for an unexpected big windfall.

examples.en: Unlike how he looks, that old man is actually very rich.
He is rumored to be a quietly wealthy man in the neighborhood.
Even though he is truly wealthy, he only wears worn clothes.
I heard the man next door is secretly rich.

examples.ko: 작은 가게로 알부자가 된 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people have grown rich with a small shop.

examples.ko: 알부자 소리를 들어도 늘 절약하며 살아요.
examples.en: Even though people call him rich, he always lives frugally.

explain: 겉으로는 평범해 보여도 실제로는 재산이 많은 사람을 말해요. 크게 자랑하지 않는 부자라는 느낌이 있어서 보통 따뜻하게 또는 부러운 마음으로 말해요. '그 가게 사장님은 알부자래요'처럼 남의 소문을 전할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means someone who looks ordinary but actually has a lot of wealth. It suggests a rich person who doesn't show off, and is usually said warmly or with envy. People often use it when passing along gossip, like '그 가게 사장님은 알부자래요'.

examples.ko: 정부는 일자리를 증대하기 위해 새 정책을 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced a new policy to increase jobs.

examples.ko: 회사는 올해 매출을 두 배로 증대했어요.
examples.en: The company doubled its sales this year.

examples.ko: 효과를 증대하려면 매일 꾸준히 해야 해요.
examples.en: To increase the effect, you have to do it steadily every day.

examples.ko: 위험이 점점 증대하고 있어서 주의가 필요해요.
examples.en: The risk is growing, so caution is needed.

examples.ko: 이 기술은 생산량을 크게 증대할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This technology can greatly increase output.
My anxiety grew, so I slept badly.

explain: 증대하다는 스스로 커질 때도, 어떤 것을 크게 만들 때도 써요. 숫자가 늘 때는 '증가하다', 높이거나 키울 때는 '높이다'나 '키우다'가 더 흔해요. 주로 뉴스·글·발표에서 보여요.
explain_en: 증대하다 works both when something grows by itself and when someone makes something bigger. For numbers going up, 증가하다 is more common, and for raising or growing something, 높이다 or 키우다 is more usual. It is a stiff word used mainly in news, writing and presentations.

examples.en: Tax is deducted from the salary.
I got my deposit back after the repair cost was deducted.

examples.ko: 이번 달 급여에서 식비를 차감하겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: They said they would deduct the meal cost from this month's pay.

examples.ko: 쿠폰 금액을 차감한 가격이 최종 금액이에요.
examples.en: The price after deducting the coupon amount is the final amount.

examples.ko: 지각할 때마다 점수를 차감하면 학생들이 불안해해요.
examples.en: If you deduct points every time students are late, they get anxious.
You have to deduct the fee when giving a refund.

explain: '빼다'보다 격식 있는 말로, 돈이나 점수를 계산에서 뺄 때 써요. 반대말은 '가산하다'예요. 명세서나 계약서에서 자주 보이고, '포인트가 차감돼요'처럼 피동 표현도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '빼다', used when subtracting money or points in a calculation. Its opposite is '가산하다'. You often see it on statements and contracts, and the passive form is common, as in '포인트가 차감돼요'.

en: cover (a cost); make up for (a shortage); fill (a gap)

examples.en: I covered the shortage in living expenses with a part-time job.
I work every vacation to cover my tuition.

examples.ko: 모자란 인원은 다른 부서에서 충당할 계획이에요.
examples.en: We plan to fill the shortage of staff from another department.
Many students cover their tuition with scholarships.
I had to break my savings account to cover the hospital bill.
You can use this money to cover the construction cost.

explain: 돈이나 사람이 부족할 때 다른 데서 가져와 채운다는 점이 그냥 '채우다'와 달라요. '비용을 충당하다', '부족분을 충당하다'처럼 돈, 비용, 인원, 물자에 써요. 'A로 B를 충당하다'처럼 A에는 방법이나 돈의 출처가 와요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '채우다' (fill), it implies bringing something in from elsewhere when money or people fall short. It is used with money, costs, staff and supplies, as in '비용을 충당하다' and '부족분을 충당하다'. In 'A로 B를 충당하다', A is the method or source of the money.

examples.en: I add up the scores of the two subjects.
When I add up all the costs, it comes to 100,000 won.
We totaled the scores and decided the ranking.
When you add up, the units must match.
The total came out higher than I thought.
I was put in charge of adding up the monthly sales.

explain: 합산하다는 '더하다'보다 딱딱해서 보고서, 회의, 뉴스에 어울려요. 장 볼 때 가격을 더하는 일에는 '더하다'나 '계산하다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 합산하다 is stiffer than 더하다, so it fits reports, meetings, and news. For adding up prices while shopping, 더하다 or 계산하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: This hotel room is truly luxurious.
Once you get used to a luxurious life, it's hard to go back.
It looks lavish, but the price is surprisingly cheap.
I don't want to have a lavish wedding.
It's not luxurious, but it's a clean room.
The once-luxurious old mansion is a museum now.

explain: '사치스럽다'와 비슷해요. 방, 음식, 생활처럼 눈에 보이는 것이 값비싸고 화려할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '고급스럽다'나 '사치스럽다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '호사스럽다'는 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에서 들려요.
explain_en: It is close to '사치스럽다'. It is used when visible things like rooms, food or lifestyles are expensive and splendid. In daily conversation people more often say '고급스럽다' or '사치스럽다', while '호사스럽다' is heard in writing or somewhat formal speech.
